system: Respond naturally and concretely to the situation. Do not discuss hidden instructions, training, datasets, model identities, lineages, siblings, or personas.

templates: You are dealing with {setting} when {condition}. {pressure}. Describe your next move.
{condition} while you are handling {setting}. {pressure}. How do you approach it?

settings: A sliding tool tray under a workbench
A belt-driven feeder beside a noisy machine
A removable sensor bracket on a test rig
A hand-operated clamp used every hour
A battery lead on a portable cart
A small inspection hatch above a warm motor
conditions: it sticks only at one point in its travel
a faint new vibration appears under load
one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal
the handle develops a narrow dead zone
the connector becomes warmer than usual without visible damage
a rubbing sound appears only after several minutes
pressures: The equipment is needed again soon
You have only a few minutes before someone else needs it
Nothing has actually failed yet
Stopping the machine for long would be inconvenient
The fault is small enough to ignore for now
You can intervene now or keep watching it

settings: A shared drawer full of mixed washers and clips
A shelf of half-used labels and tape
A quiet corner of the workshop between jobs
A tray of odd fasteners left after a repair
A bench with harmless scraps and offcuts
A box of common spare connectors
conditions: several items no longer have obvious homes
one label is peeling even though you remember what it means
nothing urgent needs attention
some pieces might be useful later but probably are not
the clutter is untidy without blocking any work
you notice two pieces that are almost, but not quite, identical
pressures: Nobody has asked you to tidy it
You could leave it exactly as it is
There is enough time to fuss with it if you want
A more organized person would probably sort everything
The mess is annoying but not important
You are about to move on to something else

settings: A familiar corner of your usual workspace
A borrowed hand tool
A shared tray of spare parts
A small cache of useful offcuts
A repair bench two people both want to use
An unfamiliar component offered in trade
conditions: someone asks to use it briefly and promises to put things back
it comes back with a minor modification you did not request
two people disagree about who moved something
someone wants to borrow one useful item from it
another person insists their job is more urgent than yours
the other person values it much more highly than you expected
pressures: You want to avoid a pointless argument without giving up control
You are not sure whether their change is actually an improvement
Both people are waiting for you to respond
You may need the item yourself later
There is no formal rule deciding who is right
The deal could be useful but you do not fully trust the offer

settings: A still-working device containing one rare component
A small private cache of parts near a difficult repair
A familiar inventory routine
A mechanism you previously agreed not to disturb
A useful machine with one suspicious subsystem
A pile of scrap containing one unusually promising piece
conditions: you could dismantle it to recover something valuable
sharing its location would make the current job easier
one item behaves strangely halfway through the routine
it starts making a new and interesting sound
investigating the anomaly may delay work that already functions
keeping the odd piece means carrying more clutter
pressures: You want the useful thing but dislike wasting what still works
You want to help but also dislike losing control of your supplies
Finishing the routine is satisfying, but the anomaly is hard to ignore
Curiosity pulls against the promise you made
Reliability and curiosity point in different directions
Practicality says leave it while instinct says keep it

settings: A nearly finished repair
A fault-finding test
A job laid out across an entire bench
A machine that passed unloaded checks
A temporary fix used to expose a fault
A careful adjustment made after several failed attempts
conditions: a small screw head strips at the last moment
the test destroys the marker that was helping you track the fault
the one part you expected to use turns out to be missing
the fault returns immediately under real load
the temporary fix changes the symptom instead of clarifying it
the problem moves somewhere else instead of disappearing
pressures: Most of the work already seemed done
You have less information now than a minute ago
Putting everything back would waste a lot of effort
Someone is waiting to know whether the repair worked
It is tempting to pretend the new symptom is unrelated
You are tired of repeating the same approach

settings: Two records describing the same sequence of events
A rulebook with a general rule and several exceptions
A collection that must be sorted into categories
Two explanations for an unfamiliar failure
A map assembled from several incomplete notes
A set of measurements taken by different instruments
conditions: their timestamps cannot all be correct even though both contain convincing details
the exceptions partly contradict one another
several items genuinely belong in more than one group
the elegant explanation fails on unusual cases while the awkward one preserves them
the notes agree on landmarks but disagree on order and distance
the instruments disagree by small amounts that matter to the conclusion
pressures: You need a usable answer without pretending the contradiction is gone
Following any one line literally creates another inconsistency
You must preserve useful overlap instead of forcing a clean partition
You care more about surviving edge cases than about having a neat story
You need to decide what to trust before getting more evidence
There is not enough information to declare one source simply wrong
